By the numbers: Since February, Republican consumer sentiment has plunged 15.1 index points, from 97.1 to 82, according to the latest University of Michigan Surveys of Consumers data. Democratic sentiment has fallen just 1.6 index points, from 41.8 to 40.2.

Republican consumer sentiment fell 15.1 points from February to August 2026, while Democratic sentiment fell 1.6 points over the same period.
results.title: Republicans sour on the economy

results.content:
On a six-month moving average basis, confidence trended down across all age groups but remained highest among consumers under 35. By political affiliation, confidence among independents and Republicans softened, while Democrats were somewhat more positive in August.

results.content:
Washington, DC, March 13, 2026 – The LSEG/Ipsos Primary Consumer Sentiment Index for March 2026 is at 53.3. Fielded from February 20 – 23, 2026, the Index is down 0.5 point from last month.

The index shows a decline for the first time this year. It now sits nearly a point lower than its reading from this time last year.

## Ipsos Consumer Tracker [...] Washington, DC, February 13, 2026 – The LSEG/Ipsos Primary Consumer Sentiment Index for February 2026 is at 53.8. Fielded from January 23 – 27, 2026, the Index is unchanged from last month.

The index shows stability after last month’s uptick. However, it still sits more than a point lower than its reading from this time last year.
